conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. I’m Dr. Patel, one of the hospitalists. You came in because of dark-brown drainage from your G-tube. Can you tell me what happened?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I woke up around 4:30 this morning and noticed the fluid in the bag was dark brown, almost reddish. It’s usually greenish-yellow. I’ve had bleeding before, so I got worried.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a good call. We checked a sample in the ER and it was guaiac positive, which means there’s blood. You’re on Lovenox for your history of blood clots—this could make bleeding more likely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Right, I’ve been on Lovenox for my upper arm clots. But I don’t feel dizzy or weak. My blood pressure should be okay, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your vitals are stable—blood pressure 116/82, heart rate 93. We drew blood, and your hemoglobin was 10.2, which is a bit low but not a big drop from your baseline. We’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that’s reassuring. But why is this happening now? I had an EGD not too long ago and they said everything looked okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did. The last one showed some irritation and redness around the G-tube site, but no active bleeding. We think this might be related to that irritation, possibly worsened by the anticoagulant.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not a new ulcer or something serious?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not that we know yet. The GI team wants to do another endoscopy to make sure. We’ll schedule that for tomorrow morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright. And my TPN? I haven’t had it since this morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re holding TPN for now since we’re checking for bleeding. Nutrition team is involved, and you’ll restart it at home with your usual 12-hour cycle.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my pain? I’ve been off morphine at home, but my belly’s been sore.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you some IV Dilaudid for breakthrough pain, but we’re not continuing it after discharge. You’re still on gabapentin and amitriptyline, which help with nerve pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s fine. I don’t want to get dependent again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We respect that. Also, social work mentioned you had some thoughts about not wanting to go on. Can you talk about that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I was overwhelmed in the ER. With everything—the pain, the bleeding, the tubes. I said things I didn’t mean. I’m not suicidal now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad to hear that. Psychiatry saw you and agreed you’re safe. We’ll keep monitoring, but you’re cleared for regular care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I just need to get through this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Quick update—we ran blood cultures and they came back with no growth. No sign of infection in your bloodstream.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. What about that Enterococcus infection from my femoral line? Am I still on antibiotics?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You completed the daptomycin course. Infectious disease reviewed it and said no further IV antibiotics are needed. You’ll keep the vancomycin lock for the line, though.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that’s one less thing to worry about.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your urine culture showed Streptococcus anginosus. It’s likely a contaminant or low-grade UTI, but since you’re not running a fever or feeling sick, we’re not treating it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I be concerned?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not right now. We’ll watch it, but it’s probably not related to your current issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your repeat blood work shows your hemoglobin is stable at 10.9. No further drop. That’s a good sign.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. When’s the endoscopy?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Scheduled for 9 a.m. You’ll be sedated, and the doctor will look for the source of the bleeding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The endoscopy is done. Good news—no active bleeding. There’s mild gastritis around the G-tube site, and some old blood, but nothing urgent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s just irritation?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. We think the G-tube is causing some chronic irritation, and the Lovenox may have triggered a small bleed. But it’s healed now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need a new tube?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not right now. The site looks clean, no infection. We’ll keep monitoring. You’ll go back to your regular ranitidine—no PPIs due to your allergy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Right, omeprazole gave me kidney issues before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Ranitidine should help reduce stomach acid and protect the lining.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better. The pain’s manageable. G-tube output is still brown, but less than before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s expected. It’ll clear over the next few days as the old blood drains out.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my Lovenox? Should I stop it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, we’re keeping it. Your history of upper extremity clots is serious. The benefit outweighs the small bleeding risk, especially now that the bleeding has stopped.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll keep using it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow. You’ll go home with your regular medications and restart TPN with home health support.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No changes to my meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: None. Same doses of gabapentin, amitriptyline, ranitidine, levothyroxine, and the rest. You’ll also keep the vancomycin lock for your line.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the Dilaudid?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re not sending it home with you. Use your oral morphine if needed, but try the other pain meds first.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set for discharge. Your condition is stable, no active bleeding, and your labs are consistent with your baseline.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call your home health team to restart TPN. If the G-tube output becomes bright red or you feel lightheaded, go to the ER.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for taking care of me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just confirming—you had a small bowel endoscopy today as part of your evaluation. It was unremarkable, no source of bleeding found beyond the mild stomach irritation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So everything’s okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. This was likely a small, self-limited bleed from G-tube irritation. With your history, we wanted to be thorough.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll document everything for your follow-up team. You’re cleared to leave once the discharge papers are ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great, thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—keep an eye on your mood. If you feel overwhelmed again, please reach out. You’re not alone.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I’m feeling much better now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Glad to hear it. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will be in with your discharge instructions and prescriptions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll wait for them.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also reviewed your hepatitis C—it’s stable, no liver issues now. Continue your usual monitoring with your specialist.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I have an appointment next month.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Stay on track with that.
